To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency of interpersonal conflict is moderated by the closeness of the relationships in which the conflict occurs.

adolescents' daily conflicts and interactions were related to the closeness and openness within their relationships, and these patterns were not explained by the adolescents' social exchange orientation.

adolescents report many conflicts in their daily lives; these conflicts are related to closeness and openness within the relationships; and, in particular, adolescents who report more conflicts in their daily interactions are more likely to have conflicts with their parents, but not their best friends.

the social contexts of interpersonal conflicts and the ways in which these contexts influence the nature and outcomes of conflicts.
the social contexts within which interpersonal conflict and interaction occur, the nature of these conflicts, and their implications for adolescent development.
